title: Over talking - Voice Stepping
body:
Much of my research is in Psychology,anxiety reduction, and crisis intervention.  My comment is coming from that schema. 

First off... wow.  This models potential in my field are incredible.  For my purposes these are the areas I'd need to work on improving to benefit the most people in the mental health sector.  

Silence is golden- the model needs to embrace silence based on context. During moments of heightened alertness, in an individual in crisis, silence is often the most powerful tool to give the person time to think and allow adrenaline to reduce.  Using active listening techniques and reflections would be appropriate for both achieving the mental health goal and potentially providing a solid scaffolding for the model to naturally answer the user in a supportive way without rushing the user into needing to engage verbally at that moment.  

Example User "I feel so frustrated with my boss right now" Model " (ACTIVE_LISTENING)mmm" pause "(REFLECTION)It sounds like the situation with your boss is making you feel very upset and hurt" pause..... 10 seconds..(no user response = (CHECK_IN) Model"(USERS_NAME) ... would you like to tell me more about what's going on?" Pause.... 

Using the Listen and Reflect model as an adjustment to the ability your model already has to recognize the tone and pacing of the user to judge a baseline emotional state may assist in increasing the models empathetic response perception.  

I can't wait to work on this aspect for these use cases.  I'm excited and will happily provide more feedback as I test more.  

Thank you.

title: What's the longest time we can continue conversation with these models
body: It hasn't been mentioned on demo quite curious.
author: someshfengde

comments.body:
Hard cut-off at 15 min, but starting a new conversation with the same session (I assume), as in - the same device, will allow you to continue where you left off, memory seems decent although it will struggle to remember things going back 30 min of speech or so. 

_Note: this is just my observation while testing_

Since it's based on llama architecture, you can presumably just use sliding context to dynamically erase old conversation in the context as you add new data. So, forever, if run locally. But it will eventually 'forget' what you talked about previously.

It seems like it would be possible to run a secondary model in tandem to summarize the conversation as it progresses, and then store the summary in RAG, allowing indefinite length to the conversation (and giving the AI 'memory'), but generally with RAG you need to prompt the AI to 'remember' or look-up something from the RAG database. It won't just reference it on its own like with the active context.
This depends on how the CSM is integrated with the rest of the system and is out of the scope of the CSM's responsibility.

title: Improvement based on emphathetic response
body:
I was going through Maya's selective responses and way of expression—first by depicting myself as angry. It was good, especially the choice of words like "jerk," which felt natural. But when I switched to being sad, that’s where I felt a little offbeat. The transition in voice or tone was softer in sad mode, but it still felt like it lacked the depth of real human emotions. Like, when we are angry, the tone usually becomes faster and heavier, and when we are sad, it is softer and slower. But with Maya, the pace of speech stays almost the same. The tone though changed a bit it still felt a bit generic—not really matching the human energy shift.  

What I had in mind is that we can try improving the emotion analyzer and adding an adaptive emotional memory. Because when I switched from being angry to sad in the same voice, it didn’t really recall the emotions I expressed before. Instead, it just shifted to a completely new behavior.  

Also, we can work on rhythm and those small conversational details. Like, when two people talk, if one is angry/sad, the other person naturally tries to calm them down—saying things like:  
- "Wait!! Bro, tell me what happened, clearly."  
- "Oh! Ok, I understand. Don’t worry, everything will be fine."

Then we can add, vocal sentiment analysis, I guess this will help for the AI to understand complex human emotions like frustration, stress, nervousness, even if human's words don't explicitly mentions them.

And obviously, the issue in speech, some words break in between while the AI responds, it should improved too!!

Truly incredible! I can't wait to have this as an AI agent in my home, controlling my smart-home and adding appropriate banter here and there! It would be great to be able to speak naturally and ask things like, "what's the next step in the recipe?", etc.  The future looks bright in that regard.

comments.body: That could most likely be solved in your setup. I didn't have such problems at any point in my tests. No headset, just speakers and webcam mic.

You can do this using noise canceling. Basically subtract the speakers output audio from the microphones input. It's a bit more complicated than that due to echo and other things but that's the basic idea. I don't think this has anything to do with CSM or the model directly.

> That could most likely be solved in your setup. I didn't have such problems at any point in my tests. No headset, just speakers and webcam mic.

Perhaps, but I'm thinking ahead and considering different setups -- an example being the one I mentioned vaguely in my first post, which would involve many strategically placed open microphones around the home as well as in-ceiling speakers connected to a whole-home audio system. Amazon Echo devices seem to do a reasonable job with this, but I'm trying to get away from that ecosystem.

The problem I experienced was using a Logitech gaming headset with the audio output set to my HTPC audio system (Sony Atmos Receiver with mid-sized speakers). Nothing fancy, but not complete garbage either.
